text.p: Everton are still searching for a new manager, the English premier league club said on Tuesday.

The club remained tight-lipped about possible successors to Joe Royle who quit three months ago and dismissed as speculation a report that Sheffield United boss Howard Kendall had been offered the job.
"If we'd appointed someone, we wouldn't be searching. I don't know of any appointment or imminent appointment," an Everton spokesman said.
TV soccer pundit and former player Andy Gray declined the job on Monday, a decision that put the club back at square one in their efforts to replace Royle.

"Following the decision of Andy Gray to turn down the opportunity to manage Everton Football Club, the board met and as a result of that meeting, the search for a new manager will continue in earnest," the spokesman said.
"The next you will hear from Everton will be the appointment of a new manager."
